source.title: On Linear Stability of SGD and Input-Smoothness of Neural Networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses flatness, generalization, and SGD's implicit regularization, and proves theoretical bounds under stated assumptions. Its experiments measure correlations between parameter and input gradient norms, not training-to-test gaps or the claim versions' outcomes.
record.gate_note: The experiments report gradient-norm correlations and their variation across learning rates and batch sizes. They do not measure generalization gaps. The paper also cites prior findings on flat minima and SGD; those cited results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional bounds connecting SGD stability, parameter gradients, input smoothness and population error. Its experiments measure gradient norms, not any version's held-out performance comparison. In particular, neither Hessian-trace flatness nor gradient-norm correlations test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its ranking of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. More precisely, the authors derive gradient-moment constraints conditional on linear stability at interpolation solutions, use multiplicative input-layer structure to bound input Sobolev seminorms, and derive population-error and robustness bounds under additional assumptions. The experiments illustrate gradient-norm correlations rather than validate held-out performance or those bounds.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a theoretical linear-stability analysis and reports gradient-norm correlation experiments; it does not reproduce the claim's natural-label test-error comparisons or the mapped interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate and batch size are varied in the gradient-norm experiments; the text reports that larger learning rates and smaller batches tend toward smaller gradient norms.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter and input gradient norms correlate across the tested networks. Larger learning rates and smaller batches tend to produce smaller norms; higher-moment correlations remain strong in most cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD settings are associated with parameter-gradient and input-gradient moments across these tested networks and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 2–6 connect assumed linear stability at interpolation solutions to gradient-moment constraints, input Sobolev seminorm bounds and a conditional population squared-error bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For models with multiplicative input-layer structure, SGD stability can bound input smoothness and population error under additional smoothness, boundedness and data-coverage assumptions.

record.problems: The experiments report scatter plots without numerical correlation values or error bars. They do not measure training-to-test gaps or evaluate the stated generalization bounds empirically. The generalization bounds depend on assumptions including interpolation, local smoothness, and a covered data distribution.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes. Experiments instead fix iteration counts and measure gradient norms.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with measured generalization gaps, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are relative to the supplied claim versions; cannot_determine does not deny the correlations explicitly reported in the text. The study's flatness quantity is an unnormalized Hessian trace, not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps and test error beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of training-to-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
